metric_rationale: The metric is the difference in TTB-consistent choice rates between non-tied conditions where tallying supports the TTB winner and conditions where tallying opposes it. TTB assigns the same binary score advantage to its winner in both sets, so it predicts a contrast near zero regardless of beta and epsilon; this within-subject subtraction also removes much of the variability caused by individual response-noise parameters. Tallying predicts a large positive contrast because its evidence points toward the TTB winner in the first set and away from that winner in the second. Pooling the three supporting and four opposing base conditions, including their reversals and repetitions, yields many observations per side and therefore a relatively stable subject-level estimate. Exact tally ties are excluded because they carry no directional tally prediction.

This metric measures behavioral alignment with the option favored by the highest-validity cue that discriminates. It is not merely an overall A/B response rate: exact stimulus reversals balance response side, so only a stimulus-contingent first-cue preference raises the score. Tallying is indifferent on every designed pair because each option wins equally many cues, predicting a match rate of 0.50. Take The Best predicts a rate above 0.50, potentially close to one depending on beta and epsilon. Averaging the diagnostic match indicator over all 96 trials gives a low-variance per-subject estimate and works identically on individual-subject and pooled data.
